title: Global Country & Territorial Jurisdiction Ontology Standard (ISO 3166-1, UN M49, Montevideo Standard)
markdown:
# Global Country & Territorial Jurisdiction Ontology Standard

**Standard Identifier:** `BIT-ONT-GEO-2026.1`  
**Governing Authorities & Registries:** ISO 3166-1:2020, UN Statistics Division (M49 Rev.4), UNTERM, Montevideo Convention on the Rights and Duties of States (1933), World Bank Group / IMF Operational Classifications (FY2026).

---

## 1. Overview & Ontological Hierarchy

Defining what constitutes a "country" or sovereign jurisdiction is one of the most foundational yet politically complex requirements in global data engineering. To guarantee mathematical reproducibility, prevent cross-border schema collisions, and enforce political neutrality across autonomous AI agents, spatial databases, and indicator pipelines, BIT establishes a **five-tier ontological hierarchy**:

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   GLOBAL GEOPOLITICAL & JURISDICTIONAL ONTOLOGY HIERARCHY                        │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  CATEGORY A: UN Member States (193 Sovereign States)                                             │
│  ├── Full de jure and de facto Westphalian sovereignty; UN Charter Chapter II compliance        │
│  └── Definitive primary keys: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, alpha-3, numeric-3 (UN M49)                   │
│                                                                                                  │
│  CATEGORY B: UN General Assembly Permanent Observer States (2 Non-Member States)                 │
│  ├── Recognized sovereign subjects of international law (Holy See, State of Palestine)           │
│  └── Full treaty-making capacity, multilateral participation, dedicated ISO/M49 entries          │
│                                                                                                  │
│  CATEGORY C: States with Partial International Recognition & De Facto Entities (10 Entities)     │
│  ├── De facto self-governing polities; varying levels of bilateral/multilateral recognition      │
│  └── Includes Associated States, disputed sovereignties, and de facto breakaway jurisdictions   │
│                                                                                                  │
│  CATEGORY D: Inhabited Dependent Territories & Special Sovereignty Jurisdictions (~50 Entities) │
│  ├── External territories, crown dependencies, overseas collectivities, autonomous areas         │
│  └── Distinct ISO 3166-1 codes tied to parent sovereign states for international reporting       │
│                                                                                                  │
│  CATEGORY E: Special Status & Supranational Entities                                             │
│  ├── Non-sovereign global commons (Antarctica / ATS) & sui generis supranational unions (EU)    │
│  └── Reserved ISO codes (AQ, EU), specialized legal regimes, non-standard statistical rules      │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## 3. Disputed Boundary & Jurisdiction Handling Principles for Agents

Autonomous agents, scrapers, and database architects must strictly adhere to the following deterministic protocol:

1. **Primary Key Invariance:** Always use **`ISO 3166-1 alpha-3`** (or `alpha-2`) and **`UN M49 numeric`** as primary database keys. Never use localized text strings or translated country names as primary join keys.
2. **Neutrality Protocol & Disputed Name Normalization:** Adhere strictly to UNTERM conventions and present dual or UN-standard naming:
   * *Falkland Islands:* `"Falkland Islands (Malvinas)"`
   * *Kosovo:* `"Kosovo (under UNSCR 1244/99)"` or `"Kosovo"` with explicit ISO user code `XK` / `XKX`
   * *Taiwan:* `"Taiwan, Province of China"`, `"Taiwan (ROC)"`, or `"Chinese Taipei"` (depending on institutional protocol: UNSD vs. World Bank/IOC/WTO)
   * *The Gulf:* `"Persian Gulf"` or `"The Gulf"` (UNTERM standard)
3. **User-Assigned Code Element Handling (ISO 3166-1 Clause 8.1.3):** For entities lacking official ISO 3166-1 assignments, agents must strictly utilize designated private-use user codes:
   * `XK` / `XKX`: Kosovo (Standardized by European Commission, IMF, World Bank, SWIFT)
   * `EU`: European Union
   * `QO`: Outlying Oceania
   * `ZZ`: Unspecified / Unknown Jurisdiction
4. **Decoupling Data Aggregation from Sovereignty Judgments:** Statistical collection must follow statistical territory definitions without implying recognition of territorial sovereignty.
